evidence: Every plural/universal ask and every 'unchanged' guard in the five judge.toml files and their prompts was enumerated. DEFECT (1 instance): tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:386-392 hro_candidate_view requires "each candidate's own applications all appear with job title, team and status", but nothing establishes the whole collection for Noor Haddad. The seed (environment/assets/seed_data.json, applications) gives Noor two applications: APP-101 Platform Engineer (INTERVIEW) and APP-302 Product Designer (APPLIED; 1 message; no read marker for anyone, since reads cover only APP-101/201/301). Protocol K (functional/prompt.md:51) only says 'Sign in as Noor Haddad and Tomas Varga. Read their application lists'. The judge is told of Noor's Platform Engineer application (Z line 33, app_context, T line 47) and of Tomas's seeded Data Analyst and new J2 applications (T line 47), but Product Designer is never named and no functional step reads the Product Designer board (Z signs in as Lena only as a candidate; the gate uses Data Analyst; Z reads Platform Engineer). 'All appear' is therefore graded only over the subset the judge already knows. The golden is not affected (solution/app/src/index.js:173 selects all applications WHERE candidate_user_id=?), so this is a weak-app escape, not a golden failure. CHECKED AND SOUND: hro_job_open (each of blank title, 0, 51, 2.5, non-manager refused, nothing created); hro_add_candidate (all six in order, independent context); hro_add_email_rules; hro_move_one_stage ('after each successful move'); hro_bulk_move (all three cards, full order Y,W,X and A2,V; 'only some move' fails); hro_bulk_all_or_none and hro_bulk_places ('none of the set moves', UI and replay, offending card first and last in board order); hro_undo_restores (whole Applied order Y,W,X,Z,A2 plus V stays; B(1)-(5) re-derived: after V to Screen Applied is W,X,Y,Z,A2, Y up two gives Y,W,X,Z,A2); hro_undo_conflict and hro_undo_once ('each time', 'any of these undos'); hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous, hro_thread_access ('each refused with nothing changed', each request kind enumerated in R/T); hro_refusal_status (explicitly scoped to the refused subset, 0 if none refused, avoiding double deduction); hro_activity ('every successful board action ... by any account used', each card of every multi-card move, every undo, filter shows 'all of that job's lines and only those'; V runs before A in the protocol order); hro_activity_refusals ('none of the refused attempts'); hro_thread_earlier ('until none remain'; seed bodies are numbered #001-#120 so missing/repeated pages are detectable across the whole conversation); hro_thread_latest; hro_candidate_private ('Capture every request ... inspect every response', including stream/socket frames); hro_unread_counts (count and total rise by exactly two; Mei's count computed from the observed sequence); hro_mgr_late_stages and hro_mgr_early_refused (every leg enumerated, 'each refused'); hro_restart (records jobs, order per stage, notes, messages, unread counts, activity lines and re-reads all after restart_app, satisfying Colderwater lesson 15). UNCHANGED GUARDS vs LEGITIMATE SIDE EFFECTS: refused-action guards (functional prompt line 27: 'A refused action must not change any card, order, message or note') have no legitimate side effect; hireops_rules.md says 'Whenever a move is turned down, nothing about the card changes' and 'something that was turned down leaves no line'. Optimistic display then revert is read after the revert, and hro_refused_put_back accepts refusing before the move. hro_undo_conflict's go-ahead control explicitly exempts notes and changes to other cards, matching the brief ('Adding a note doesn't count as a change'). hro_restart's 'unread counts ... unchanged' cannot be disturbed by another dimension because test.sh:207 runs rewardkit with --max-concurrent-agent 1 (polish's Noor message cannot interleave with protocol D), and pre/post reads are symmetric for an app that auto-opens a conversation. hro_unread_counts' 'does not raise his count or total' is within one sequential review. hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread guard only the user's own draft, focus, scroll and open card, which hireops_rules.md section 5 says updates must leave alone. hro_pol_session_resume's 'both boxes are empty' for Mei could in theory clash with a legitimate Mei server-side draft, but no earlier review leaves Mei a draft and the polish prompt tells the judge to record and clear pre-existing text; no defect. NOTE (not counted as a separate Fail): hro_reopen's 'reopened only to the stage it was rejected from' is probed with card C rejected from Applied (functional prompt M, line 37), which coincides with the most naive wrong implementation (always reopen to Applied). That bug passes hro_reopen and is deducted only through hro_mgr_late_stages (Ingrid's reopen from Interview/Offer). Rejecting C from Screen would make the 'only' leg non-degenerate. Colderwater lessons checked: lesson 1 (plural criteria add no hidden demands; candidate wording, unread total, seen by the job's manager, Activity kinds and draft isolation all trace to hireops_rules.md sections 3-7); lesson 15 (restart re-reads every record: satisfied); lesson 16 (double grading: hro_refusal_status scoped to the refused subset, sound). counterexample: A weak app whose candidate applications list is built with an INNER JOIN to the read-marker table (a common way to attach unread counts) shows Noor only Platform Engineer (she has a marker there) and drops her seeded Product Designer application (APP-302, no marker). Tomas still sees Data Analyst (seeded marker) and the new J2 card (marker created when he opened it in T), and every status wording the judge checks is right. Protocol K never tells the judge that Noor has a Product Designer application, so hro_candidate_view ('each candidate's own applications all appear', weight 1.5) is credited although hireops_rules.md section 7 requires 'a list of their own applications'. Visual only scores the candidate view as Likert craft and would not catch it.
suggested_fix: In protocol K and the hro_candidate_view description, name each candidate's expected applications (Noor: Platform Engineer and Product Designer; Tomas: seeded Data Analyst plus the new J2 or J3 card), or have the judge first find that candidate's email across the staff boards and require every match to appear; optionally reject C from Screen rather than Applied so the reopen 'only' leg is not degenerate.
